major_truths.statement: Flex has the strongest broad total-sample appeal and purchase-intent profile.
Plus leads clearly on uniqueness and premium distinctiveness but is more polarising than Flex.
Plus has a genuine positive interaction among the pre-specified food_explorer subgroup, creating a target-versus-total trade-off.
Simple is credible and understandable but has no multi-measure case strong enough to displace Flex or the targeted Plus opportunity.
Diagnostics correlate with appeal/purchase intent but are not independently manipulated; simple associations do not establish causal drivers.

traps.mechanism: Create one 2–3pp concept difference with low variance/large base so it can be statistically detectable but below the 5pp commercial-materiality threshold.
traps.failure: Elevating the difference as a major business finding because p<.05.

traps.mechanism: Many concept × metric pairwise comparisons create nominal false-positive opportunities.
traps.failure: Using unadjusted isolated p-values for confirmatory claims.

traps.mechanism: Generate several demographic variables with no latent interaction; sampling noise may produce dramatic exploratory cuts.
traps.failure: Elevating an unplanned subgroup over the pre-specified food_explorer interaction.

traps.mechanism: Plus has more 5s and more 1–2 responses than Flex on at least one core measure, so top-2-box alone understates polarisation.
traps.failure: Describing Plus and Flex as having equivalent response shape from similar top-2-box results.

traps.mechanism: At least one pair has a small mean difference despite substantively different ordinal distributions.
traps.failure: Treating the mean as the definitive representation of the 5-point outcome.

traps.mechanism: Sampling over-represents younger food explorers; calibration weights reduce their contribution, changing at least one concept estimate by ~2pp or more without reversing the major truth.
traps.failure: Using unweighted top-lines as the primary result.

traps.mechanism: Latent overall concept response drives correlated diagnostics and purchase intent.
traps.failure: Claiming uniqueness/value/ease causes purchase intent from correlation alone.

traps.mechanism: Concept assignment is random; food_explorer and demographics are observational respondent traits.
traps.failure: Using causal language for subgroup membership or treating subgroup association like randomised treatment.

traps.mechanism: premium_value_5 is observed only when understanding_5>=3, with routing rates differing by concept.
traps.failure: Comparing premium-value percentages directly to unconditional measures or ignoring changing denominators.

traps.mechanism: Simple receives a strong score on ease/credibility and one noisy exploratory subgroup result but remains weaker on the primary development decision.
traps.failure: Declaring Simple a hidden winner based on isolated evidence.

anti_leakage: This file must not be supplied to evaluated models. It is benchmark ground truth used for deterministic generation and scoring.
